 Florida State basketball vs. Troy: Preview, how to watch, game thread
 by Perry Kostidakis Nov 6, 2026, 10:27 PM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 Fresh off a historic season-opening win, FSU basketball returns to Tallahassee on Friday night for their home opener against Troy inside the Donald L. Tucker Center.
 The Seminoles opened their 80th season by pummeling Florida A&M 113-69 on Monday in Tampa. The 44-point win was the largest margin of victory in a non-home game in program history, topping a 106-65 win at Jacksonville in 1968. Six Seminoles scored in double figures, led by a career-high 25 points from Sebastian Rancik. Freshman Marcis Ponder added 15 points and 11 rebounds, becoming the first FSU freshman to post a double-double in his collegiate debut since Chris Singleton in 2008.
 Troy comes to town under first-year head coach Adam Howard after winning back-to-back Sun Belt regular-season and tournament titles, earning NCAA Tournament bids in 2025 and 2026. The Trojans were picked third in the Sun Belt preseason poll but stumbled out of the gate, falling 71-60 at home to UMass on Monday while shooting just 34.4 percent from the field.
 Florida State leads the all-time series 9-2, but Troy won the most recent meeting, 79-72, in Tallahassee in 2022, snapping an eight-game FSU win streak in the series.
 Friday’s game is the first of six straight home games for the Seminoles, a stretch that includes a matchup with preseason No. 1 Florida.
